channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: US Jobs Surge Raises Odds of December Fed Hike
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Economics Chief US Economist Anna Wong says October's surprisingly strong jobs report showed hiring broadening into white collar, manufacturing and transportation jobs, strengthening the case for another Federal Reserve rate hike. Wong tells hosts Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo how the Bloomberg Price Project uses millions of alternative data points to provide an independent, more granular measure of US inflation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Berkshire Hathaway’s Operating Earnings Fall, Buybacks Rise
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway Inc.’s operating earnings fell to $12.7 billion in the third quarter, a 5.8% decline from a year earlier, the Omaha, Nebraska-based conglomerate said Saturday in a statement.
item.dc:creator: Alex Rajbhandari

item.title: Crypto’s Trump-Fueled Washington Boom Reaches Its Endgame
item.description: Crypto’s extraordinary run of political good fortune in Washington has come to an abrupt halt. With Democrats set to control Congress following their midterm sweep, the industry faces the prospect of tougher rules and closer scrutiny of its ties to President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Teresa Xie and Scott Patterson

item.title: Trafigura Snaps Up Copper in Asia as China Faces Supply Crunch
item.description: Trafigura Group has been buying large volumes of copper to boost sales into Asia as local supplies run low, adding to a scramble for metal that’s pushed regional premiums for spot cargoes to record highs.
item.dc:creator: Julian Luk, Jack Farchy and Alfred Cang

item.title: Why India’s Stock Markets Hold a Session on Diwali: Explainer
item.description: India’s stock markets will open for a special shortened session on Sunday as the country celebrates Diwali, its biggest festival, keeping alive a tradition that has survived the shift from handwritten ledgers and bustling trading floors to smartphones and algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Samie Modak

item.title: China Extends Gold-Buying Streak to Two Years as Prices Drop
item.description: China’s central bank added to its gold reserves in October — extending a buying streak to two years — as the precious metal fell almost 7% to end the month below the $4,000-an-ounce support threshold.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie

item.title: Beijing Vows to Hit Back Against US Sanctions on China Companies
item.description: China strongly opposes US sanctions on two Chinese companies over their dealings with a third party and reserves the right to take “necessary measures” to protect its interests, China’s Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: The Corner Store Brings Its New York Experience to the Las Vegas Strip
item.description: Catch Hospitality Group is opening a Las Vegas location of The Corner Store at the Cosmopolitan. Co-Founder and Partner Eugene Remm says the 150-seat restaurant will preserve the intimacy and authentic SoHo experience of its 75-seat New York original, rather than offer a Vegas-specific or watered-down version. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Elanco Shares Jump After Q3 Beat and Outlook Raise
item.description: Elanco Animal Health shares rose nearly 8% after the company reported third-quarter earnings above expectations and raised its full-year outlook. Jeff Simmons, Elanco’s President and CEO, called it a high-quality quarter, citing 11% reported growth and broad strength across markets and product lines. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kailey Leinz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sweetgreen CEO Says Sales Rebound After Cyclospora-Related Traffic Drop
item.description: Sweetgreen CEO and Co-Founder Jonathan Neman says that sales momentum has improved after a summer Cyclospora outbreak—unrelated to Sweetgreen’s stores but damaging to traffic across the sector. The company reported October comparable sales growth of about 5%, following a return to flat comps in September, and saw further improvement in early November. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kailey Leinz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: FIGS Beats Earnings as Demand Outstrips Supply, CEO Trina Spear Says
item.description: FIGS reported third-quarter top- and bottom-line results above expectations, with revenue of $190.7 million versus an estimate of $182.8 million. The company logged a fourth consecutive quarter of at least 25% revenue growth; non-scrubwear revenue rose 35%, and international revenue also increased. CEO and co-founder Trina Spear said health care professionals are expanding their FIGS purchases beyond scrubs to items such as underscrubs, compression socks and outerwear, for work and off-duty wear. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kailey Leinz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI-Generated Movie Heading Theaters
item.description: Artificial intelligence is moving from experimental videos to the big screen. Fable Studio CEO Edward Saatchi says a team of just 30 people spent nine months creating Gods Don’t Give Gifts, an AI-generated animated feature that still relies on human directors, writers, voice actors and artists. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss how AI changes the filmmaking process and what it means for Hollywood's traditional production model. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Providing Capital to Tech Companies: Masters In Business with Ann Berry
item.description: Barry speaks with Ann Berry, founder and managing partner of Threadneedle. They discuss her path from Goldman Sachs M&A and private equity to running a hospitality services company through the pandemic. They also discuss Ann's early-stage bets on AI and deepfake detection, and surveying the expanding IPO landscape. (Source: Bloomberg)

They also discuss Ann's early-stage bets on AI and deepfake detection, and surveying the expanding IPO landscape. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Airbnb Surges 12% as Growth Accelerates and Outlook Rises | Closing Bell
item.description: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Kailey Leinz, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hedge Funds Fled Bullish Oil Bets Ahead of Election Day Drop
item.description: Hedge funds cut bullish crude bets by the most since June as the US and Iran struck rare de-escalatory notes, positioning them to profit from the selloff after the Democratic sweep of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Lorelei Smillie and Mia Gindis

item.title: Braskem Owners Pull Funding Offer as Debt Talks Hit Snag
item.description: Talks between Brazil’s Braskem SA and its creditors regarding an out-of-court debt rework have soured, with shareholders taking a proposed capital injection key to a deal off the table if talks stand as they are, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Mariana Durao and Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo

item.title: Canadian Dollar Notches Worst Week Since September on Weak Jobs
item.description: The Canadian dollar posted its biggest weekly loss since late September after weaker-than-expected domestic employment data reinforced concerns about the outlook for the country’s economy.
item.dc:creator: Melos Ambaye

item.title: How a Bank Scandal Is Taking Down Trump’s Ally in Paraguay
item.description: Officials at the Inter-American Development Bank’s investment arm suspected something was off almost as soon as they walked through the doors of Paraguay’s Ueno Bank SA.
item.dc:creator: Manuela Tobias and Ignacio Olivera Doll

item.title: Gold Extends Drop on Stronger-Than-Expected US Employment Data
item.description: Gold fell after a hot US nonfarm payrolls print added fuel to speculations that the Federal Reserve will seek to raise interest rates to contain inflation.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ryan and Preeti Soni
